FINDING_ID: IM_F019  
SEVERITY: 0.56  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `dynamic_management.py`, top module docstring, compatibility claim and import examples. The shim promises “existing imports continue to work unchanged” but only demonstrates class-style imports for `DynamicManager`. Within the stated immune boundary, several exported names are constants/functions rather than classes, notably `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS`, `apply_diagnosis`, `_apply_transform`, and possibly `process_round` if previously imported as a symbol. This is not the same as prior findings that those names are missing from the actual import surface; the missed issue is that the compatibility contract is under-specified at the usage level. A backward-compatibility shim must document both object availability and supported import forms. Evidence: the docstring contains only these examples: `from dynamic_management import DynamicManager` and `from bench.dynamic_management import DynamicManager`, while the same docstring’s module inventory explicitly names non-class immune symbols in `_manager.py`.  
FIX: Replace the examples block in the module docstring with explicit immune-symbol examples covering class, function, and constant imports. Exact replacement:  
<<<<
them so that existing imports continue to work unchanged:

    from dynamic_management import DynamicManager       # runners (bench/ CWD)
    from bench.dynamic_management import DynamicManager  # tests (repo root CWD)
====
them so that existing imports continue to work unchanged for all public API
shapes (classes, functions, and constants), for example:

    from dynamic_management import DynamicManager
    from dynamic_management import DetectorHealthMonitor, FailureHandler
    from dynamic_management import _REMEDIATION_CHAINS, apply_diagnosis

    from bench.dynamic_management import DynamicManager
    from bench.dynamic_management import DetectorHealthMonitor, FailureHandler
    from bench.dynamic_management import _REMEDIATION_CHAINS, apply_diagnosis
>>>>
FOLLOW: This fix increases the specificity of the compatibility contract and therefore exposes a downstream inconsistency in the actual orchestrator import block, which currently re-exports only `DynamicManager`. If the documentation is corrected as above, the code must also re-export `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS`, `apply_diagnosis`, and `_apply_transform` to remain truthful. That downstream code/export mismatch is already independently identified by prior findings; this documentation fix does not create a new behavioural defect, but it removes ambiguity and makes the existing export defect impossible to miss.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Apply the docstring replacement above.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

DESCRIPTION: FIND: `dynamic_management.py`, immune-boundary framing in the module docstring omits `_failure_handler.py` from the review boundary while the analytical boundary and the shim’s own imports place `FailureHandler` and `CorrelatedFailureModel` in the immune layer. Prior findings noted this as a boundary mismatch in general. The missed issue is the practical consequence for review completeness: the file’s own decomposition guidance directs a reviewer to inspect `_types.py + _immune.py + _manager.py` only, which excludes the only module that likely implements timeout/underperformance/failure escalation logic tied to immune config parameters (`timeout_multiplier`, `theta_under`, `n_fail`, `persistence_window`, `eta_underperform`, `k_min`). Evidence: docstring line “The immune layer review boundary is: _types.py + _immune.py + _manager.py.” contrasted with the explicit immune-layer import block immediately below importing `FailureHandler` and `CorrelatedFailureModel` from `_failure_handler.py`.  
FIX: Replace the boundary sentence with one that includes `_failure_handler.py` and distinguishes detection from remediation/orchestration. Exact replacement:  
<<<<
The immune layer review boundary is: _types.py + _immune.py + _manager.py.
====
The immune layer review boundary is: _types.py + _immune.py +
_failure_handler.py + _manager.py. Review `_immune.py` for detector health,
`_failure_handler.py` for failure classification/escalation, and `_manager.py`
for remediation orchestration (`_REMEDIATION_CHAINS`, `apply_diagnosis`,
`_apply_transform`, `process_round` integration).
>>>>
FOLLOW: This fix changes the declared ownership map of the immune subsystem and therefore has downstream documentation impact on any reviewer instructions, task packets, or test comments that currently treat `_failure_handler.py` as outside the immune boundary. It also sharpens responsibility boundaries for config parameters: failure-detection thresholds now clearly belong to `_failure_handler.py`, while remediation state belongs to `_immune.py`/`_manager.py`. No code behaviour changes are introduced, but any supplementary interface summary should be updated to include `_failure_handler.py` as part of the immune review set.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Apply the boundary sentence replacement above.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F022  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `dynamic_management.py`, there is no explicit public grouping or alias for the immune subsystem even though the file is being used as a compatibility surface for a decomposed monolith. The immune API is scattered across four blocks: `_types` (`DetectorDiagnosis`, enums, result types), `_immune` (`DetectorHealthMonitor`), `_failure_handler` (`FailureHandler`, `CorrelatedFailureModel`), and `_manager` (only `DynamicManager`, despite the docstring naming other immune symbols). This is a missed interface defect at the shim level: a caller cannot determine immune API completeness by inspecting one section because immune-relevant names are fragmented and partially hidden behind generic headings. Evidence: the “Immune layer” block does not include `DetectorDiagnosis` even though it is in-scope, and the orchestrator block does not expose the immune orchestration helpers named in the inventory.  
FIX: Reorganize the shim imports so the immune public surface is declared contiguously and explicitly. Exact replacement for the immune/orchestrator-related blocks:  
<<<<
# ── Immune layer ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from bench.dm._immune import DetectorHealthMonitor  # noqa: F401
from bench.dm._failure_handler import (  # noqa: F401
    FailureHandler,
    CorrelatedFailureModel,
)

# ── Event stream ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from bench.dm._events import ManagerEventStream  # noqa: F401

# ── Orchestrator ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from bench.dm._manager import DynamicManager  # noqa: F401
====
# ── Immune layer ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Public immune API spans shared types, detector health, failure handling,
# and manager remediation/orchestration hooks.
from bench.dm._immune import DetectorHealthMonitor  # noqa: F401
from bench.dm._failure_handler import (  # noqa: F401
    FailureHandler,
    CorrelatedFailureModel,
)
from bench.dm._manager import (  # noqa: F401
    DynamicManager,
    _REMEDIATION_CHAINS,
    apply_diagnosis,
    _apply_transform,
)

# ── Event stream ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from bench.dm._events import ManagerEventStream  # noqa: F401
>>>>
FOLLOW: This fix has two downstream consequences. First, it makes the shim’s section structure consistent with the analytical boundary, reducing the chance of accidental omission during future refactors. Second, if `_manager.py` does not actually expose `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS`, `apply_diagnosis`, or `_apply_transform` at module scope, this import will fail, revealing a deeper export/ownership bug rather than silently masking it. That failure would be desirable because the current shim already advertises those symbols in documentation.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Apply the import-block replacement above.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

DESCRIPTION: FIND: `dynamic_management.py`, the phrase “All classes, functions, and constants that were previously defined in this 6,890-line monolith are now in bench/dm/ submodules” is too broad for the immune boundary because the shim itself demonstrates a split public/private policy that is not explained. It re-exports some underscore-prefixed internals from `_convergence` but not underscore-prefixed `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS` from `_manager`. Prior findings covered the concrete export mismatch. The missed issue is the top-level documentation inconsistency: the file claims a universal re-export policy for prior symbols, but the visible import choices show selective, undocumented curation. Evidence: `_finding_similarity`, `_tokenize_for_similarity`, `_bigrams`, `_STOPWORDS` are re-exported; `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS` is not.  
FIX: Narrow the universal claim to an explicit public-API claim and note that some internal helpers are intentionally not re-exported unless listed. Exact replacement:  
<<<<
All classes, functions, and constants that were previously defined in this
6,890-line monolith are now in bench/dm/ submodules. This file re-exports
them so that existing imports continue to work unchanged for all public API
shapes (classes, functions, and constants), for example:
====
Public API symbols previously imported from the monolith now live in
bench/dm/ submodules. This shim re-exports the supported compatibility
surface listed below so that existing public imports continue to work
unchanged, for example:
>>>>
FOLLOW: This fix requires a downstream cleanup of the shim’s actual export surface to align with the phrase “supported compatibility surface listed below.” In particular, either private convergence helpers should be documented as intentionally supported, or they should be removed from the shim. That downstream inconsistency is already reflected in prior findings. No runtime impact identified from the text change alone.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Apply the docstring replacement above.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
